Estimate note: Amorphous bars soften over a narrow range near Tg, so the two loads sit close
Reason words: its HDT at 1.8 MPa, a harsher load
Basis: A bar deflects at a lower temperature under a heavier load, so a product's HDT at 1.8 MPa is a floor for its HDT at 0.45 MPa in the same state (PR08, and hdt045's Lower bound in headline_definitions.csv: one relation in three agreeing places, LEDGER-LB-DRIFT). The screening review's experts found it in every same-sheet pair but one, by 1 °C (C22, V12).

Applies to: Base polymer: PET | PETG | PP | PE | PPS | PVDF | PC | PC-PBT
Estimate note: Not applicable
Reason words: its modulus after conditioning in humid air, which counts as dry for a plastic that takes up almost no water
Basis: A plastic that takes up negligible water is as stiff conditioned at laboratory humidity as dry: BASF Ultrafuse PET CF15's printed bars were conditioned 72 h at 23 °C and 50 % RH (C23, V17). A plastic takes up negligible water, by the executor's ruling of 2026-10-18 (D153), where its registered source in polymers.csv prints a saturated uptake of at most 0.5 % to ISO 62, or, where it prints only a 24-hour figure, at most 0.15 % in 24 h: PE below 0.01 % at saturation (R-MCAM-PROTEUS-HDPE-DS), PP below 0.1 % (R-MCAM-PROTEUS-PP-H-DS), PPS 0.10 % to ISO 62 (R-MCAM-TECHTRON-1000-PPS-DS), PVDF 0.03 % at equilibrium immersed (R-ARKEMA-KYNAR-710-TDS), PC 0.30 % (R-COVESTRO-MAKROLON-2405-ISO), PET 0.50 % to ISO 62 (R-MCAM-ERTALYTE-PET-P-DS; its 0.9 % to ASTM D570 is another, longer immersion method), PETG 0.13 % in 24 h (R-EASTMAN-EASTAR-6763-TDS) and PC-PBT 0.080 % in 24 h (R-SABIC-XENOY-6620-DS). Not ABS (1 %), ASA, PC-ABS (0.7 %), POM, the elastomers or any polyamide. No product here prints both a dry and a conditioned modulus of one of these polymers on one sheet, so the row rests on those sources and on the experts' pairs.

Estimate note: Annealed after printing: a crystallising matrix deflects tens of degrees higher (11 grades that publish both: median +52 C, +28 to +108; D162)
Basis: Annealing crystallises a printed bar and raises its heat deflection, never lowers it: in every same-sheet pair of an as-printed and an annealed HDT the annealed one is at least as high (the experts' 11 of 11, C24, V13). So an annealed HDT is the most the product reaches as printed: it may fail a minimum for the printed part, never pass one.

Estimate note: Annealed after printing: a crystallising matrix stiffens, about 11 % (13 grades that publish both: median x1.11, 1.05 to 1.35; D162)
Basis: Annealing changes a printed bar's stiffness in either direction: the experts' pair sets disagree (17 of 17 rose in one; x0.79 to x1.12 in the other, C24, V13). BASF's PAHT CF15 sheet prints 8.386 GPa dry as printed and 6.588 GPa dry annealed, a ratio of 1.273, the largest same-sheet pair in this database; so an annealed modulus bounds the printed part only from above, after multiplying by 1.28.

Applies to: Base polymer: PLA | PLA blend | PLA-PHA | PET
Estimate note: Not applicable
Reason words: its HDT on a moulded bar or one its sheet does not describe
Basis: PLA and PET print glassy but can crystallise: a moulded bar cooled slowly in a hot tool is crystalline and a print is not, so an HDT from a moulded bar, or one whose sheet does not describe it, is at most what the printed part reaches (C35, V19). Such a value stays the product's value and in its material's spread, but may only fail a minimum, never pass one. PLA-PHB is not named: polymers.csv records it as crystallising while printing (its own sheet gives 119 °C as printed, with no need for annealing), which keeps the acceptance of undescribed bars, as for the nylons and PP (D84). PETG and PCTG cannot crystallise and keep it too.

Estimate note: XY is typically about 1.4 times Z
Reason words: its modulus pulled across its layers (Z)
Basis: A bar pulled across its layers is held by the bonds between them, and is not meaningfully stiffer than one pulled along them: XY is at least 0.79 x Z on every same-sheet pair in this database (the lowest, Polymaker PolyMide PA6 GF conditioned after annealing, 2.053 against 2.593 GPa). The experts measured Z/XY up to 1.07 (C31).

Estimate note: Not applicable
Reason words: its modulus after conditioning in humid air
Basis: A nylon takes up water from humid air and softens: its conditioned stiffness is at most its dry one (conditioned/dry 0.27 to 1.0 on the pairs the experts found, C31). So a conditioned modulus is a floor for the dry part.

Applies to: Morphology: amorphous | semicrystalline | not modelled; Modifier / filler: Aramid fibre | Carbon fibre | Ceramic | Commercial variant / undisclosed | ESD formulation | Electrically conductive | Glass fibre | Glass spheres | Graphene | Metal powder | Natural fibre | PTFE | Unfilled / unspecified
Estimate note: Flexural and tensile moduli of a printed bar agree to within about 20%
Basis: A bar's tensile modulus lies between 0.46 and 1.91 times its flexural modulus on every same-sheet pair of solid bars in this database where the tensile value is measured the way the headline asks: the lowest Creality Hyper-PLA+ (1.146 against 2.490 GPa), the highest colorFabb PETG Economy (1.93 against 1.0 GPa) and XT-CF20 (5.15 against 2.7 GPa). The screening review's band, 0.70 to 1.59 (the middle 95 % of the materials scientist's 482 pairs, C31), is narrower, and ten pairs here lie outside it, five above: it would fail a product like XT-CF20 at 5 GPa. A band decides only when wholly on one side. Elastomers are left out, as PR07 leaves them out (a rubber's bending and pulling stiffness are not ordered the same way), and so are foamed filaments, whose foamed core bends far more easily than it pulls (colorFabb's Lightweight PET FLEX: 1.5 against 0.523 GPa).

Estimate note: Across the layers strength is typically 60% of XY, with a wide spread
Reason words: its strength pulled across its layers (Z)
Basis: A bar pulled across its layers breaks at the bonds between them, and is not meaningfully stronger than one pulled along them: XY is at least 0.86 x Z on every same-sheet pair in this database (the lowest, a TPI at 83 against 96 MPa). The experts measured Z/XY strength up to 1.11 (C31).

Estimate note: Break strain is never below the yield strain, and a ductile bar goes far beyond it
Basis: A bar yields before it breaks, so its elongation at break is at least its elongation at yield (PR05, and elongationXY's Lower bound in headline_definitions.csv, LEDGER-LB-DRIFT).

Basis: The strain at the maximum stress is reached on the way to break, so the elongation at break is at least it (PR10, and elongationXY's Lower bound in headline_definitions.csv, LEDGER-LB-DRIFT).
